elements.element: The liability cap must apply mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The clause limits “EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY” using the same cap.

elements.element: The fee limb must include fees paid.
elements.evidence: The cap expressly includes “fees paid.”

elements.element: The fee limb must include fees payable.
elements.evidence: The cap expressly includes fees “payable,” rather than only amounts actually paid.

elements.element: The fee limb must use total fees rather than fees for only the transaction giving rise to liability.
elements.evidence: The revised text uses “THE TOTAL AMOUNT OF fees” and removes the original limitation to amounts paid “FOR THE TRANSACTION” to which liability relates.

elements.element: The fee-measurement period must be the 12 months preceding the claim.
elements.evidence: The clause specifies “fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim.”

elements.element: The cap must be the greater of the 12-month fee limb and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The cap is expressly “THE GREATER OF (A)” the fee limb “AND (B) USD 1,000,000.”

elements.element: Indirect damages must be excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that neither party has liability to the other for “ANY INDIRECT” damages.

elements.element: Consequential damages must be excluded mutually.
elements.evidence: The clause provides that neither party has liability to the other for “CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES.”

elements.element: Either party's breach of confidentiality obligations must be excluded from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the liability cap does not apply to “either party's breach of its confidentiality” obligations.

elements.element: Either party's breach of data protection obligations must be excluded from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the liability cap does not apply to breach of “data protection” obligations.

elements.element: Either party's breach of security obligations must be excluded from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the liability cap does not apply to breach of “security obligations.”

elements.element: Either party's indemnification obligations must be excluded from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the liability cap does not apply to “its indemnification obligations.”

elements.element: Either party's gross negligence must be excluded from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the liability cap does not apply to “its gross negligence.”

elements.element: Either party's wilful misconduct must be excluded from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the liability cap does not apply to “willful misconduct”; the spelling difference is immaterial.

elements.element: Either party's fraud must be excluded from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the liability cap does not apply to “fraud.”

elements.element: Either party's infringement of the other party's intellectual property must be excluded from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the liability cap does not apply to “its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights.”

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations must not be treated as damages for purposes of the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly provides that “Customer's payment obligations … are not damages for purposes of this Section 9.”

elements.element: The liability cap must apply mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: The clause applies the cap to “EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY.”

elements.element: The liability cap must equal 12 months' fees.
elements.evidence: The cap is the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, so it does not equal 12 months' fees when that fee amount is below USD 1,000,000.

elements.element: Either party's indemnification obligations must be excluded from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The cap does not apply to “either party's … indemnification obligations.”

elements.element: Either party's breach of confidentiality obligations must be excluded from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The cap does not apply to “either party's breach of its confidentiality” obligations.

elements.element: Either party's gross negligence must be excluded from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The cap does not apply to “either party's … gross negligence.”

elements.element: Either party's wilful misconduct must be excluded from the liability cap.
elements.evidence: The cap does not apply to “either party's … willful misconduct.”

result.reason: The operative language satisfies every preferred requirement, including the mutual greater-of cap, mutual damages exclusion, all required uncapped carve-outs, and treatment of Customer payment obligations. Assessed independently, the fallback is not fully satisfied because its cap must equal 12 months' fees, whereas this clause imposes a USD 1,000,000 floor. The redline is not strictly minimal because “and all amounts due from Corio under this Agreement” is broader than the required exclusion for Customer payment obligations and could encompass other liabilities. The clause otherwise preserves the intended limitation-of-liability structure, but drafting quality is materially reduced by awkward residual text (“the claim TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES”), inconsistent capitalization, and the unnecessarily broad Corio formulation.
